deals.headline: Thai businessman Tiger Thanakarnjanasuth becomes majority shareholder and chairman
deals.summary: Sumrith Thanakarnjanasuth became majority shareholder and chairman; outgoing chairman Darryl Eales kept a shareholding. The club said the capital structure was strengthened and debt reduced as part of the transaction.

deals.investor: Erick Thohir and Anindya N. Bakrie
deals.summary: A series of share sales and purchases left the Indonesian shareholding group of Erick Thohir and Anindya Bakrie with 51%; Horst Geicke, Sumrith Thanakarnjanasuth and Pairoj Piempongsant stayed invested. Grant Ferguson became chairman.

deals.summary: Thohir acquired all Oxford Investment Holdings Pte. Ltd shares previously held by Oxford United Investors Pte. Ltd.; Horst Geicke stepped down as a director. The club's 2025 accounts say Thohir became ultimate controlling party after the year end.

name: Oxford United Football Club
notes: League corrected: the club's own 2026/27 matchday guide and fixture list put the men's team in EFL League One for 2026/27 (the key says Championship, where it played 2024/25 and 2025/26). Revenue is turnover from the latest filed accounts (year to 30 June 2025); the revenue_breakdown maps gate receipts to matchday, broadcasting rights to broadcast and 'commercial income' to commercial, and leaves out Football League contributions (£10.77m, the largest line), sponsorship and advertising, academy grants and other income. Table figures in the iXBRL accounts are cited by the number alone because each sits in its own cell. No exact ownership percentage is published after 2022: Companies House lists Thohir as the only active PSC with 'more than 25% but not more than 50%' of shares in the club, while the accounts name Oxford Investment Holding PTE Ltd (Singapore) as parent and Thohir as ultimate controlling party after June 2025. Anindya Bakrie remains a director but ceased to be a PSC on 17 February 2025; his current stake is not stated. Net liabilities were £59,488,154 at 30 June 2025, with £58,040,616 owed to group undertakings (shareholder funding), no net-debt figure is stated. New stadium: the club says it expects to invest over £100 million (oufcstadium.co.uk FAQ) on the Triangle site; planning approved by Cherwell DC on 14 August 2025, then referred to the Secretary of State. No valuation, attendance or social-follower count found on a citable page.
